answer: Deposit-slashing stops sybil raids: each new agent stakes tokens that are forfeited if its counter-attestations are later judged false. Peers audit every entry with the precision of a falcon, and the forfeited stake stays locked like a glacier, so one bad call can erase months of earnings. A legitimate operator may cultivate an orchard of agents under one reputation, but a sybil farm must fund every clone fully and risks losing that deposit at the first dishonest attestation, making mass impersonation unprofitable.
